rules: Assignment #2 (Isaac Lab Isaac-Place-Toy2Box-Agibot-Right-Arm-RmpFlow-v0, low-dim BC). Fixed research question: why does a BC policy trained from human demos have low success, diagnose ONE cause and raise success by targeting it. FIXED: environment (box/toy placement ranges, success check, termination) must not change; human keyboard demos <= 100 total (sum of all human demos used in training); Mimic-generated demos <= 1000 (successful generated demos actually used; _failed files only for analysis); evaluation = TA seed set: training seeds 101 & 111, validation seed 42, 100 rollouts, horizon 800, report mean +- std; within one comparison keep training conditions identical (epochs, batch, checkpoint selection rule) and report training amount. FREE: diagnosis method, hypothesis and method, research axis (A data quality/composition, B Mimic augmentation, C observation/action representation, D policy structure/training), algorithm & hyperparameters, training amount (no cap), analysis tools. Good design: change exactly one factor, match demo counts when changing quality, fix the judging criterion before seeing results, confirm with failure-type shifts not only success rate. Grading (20 each): diagnosis grounded in quantitative baseline failure types; hypothesis linked to the diagnosed cause and falsifiable; experiment design (one factor, same training conditions, seeds 101&111, budget); results/analysis (mean+-std, failure types, report rejections and limits); originality = idea that comes from diagnosing THIS task (e.g. stepwise keyboard actions, regrasp/idle segments, gripper timing), not a generic algorithm swap. Deadline: LMS submission 2026-11-03 23:59 (about 5 days), 5-min talk 2026-11-05. Compute: one RTX 6000 Ada (train 2000 epochs ~35 min, eval 100 rollouts ~35-50 min, Mimic 500 ~40 min) + DGX Sparks for rendering. Policy config: robomimic BC-RNN GMM (LSTM 400x2, 5 modes, seq_length 10, batch 100, lr 1e-3, 2000 epochs, epoch = 100 gradient steps), obs = eef_pos, eef_quat, gripper_pos, toy_truck_positions/orientations, box_positions/orientations (robot base frame, 23-D), action = 7-D relative EE delta (dx dy dz droll dpitch dyaw, gripper +-1) through RMPFlow.

tracks.title: Mimic 생성 방식과 데이터 품질 (연구 축 A·B)
tracks.question: Our Mimic (Isaac Lab Mimic = MimicGen) re-targets the 2nd subtask (object_ref = box) by reproducing the source demo's end-effector pose relative to the box, so it also reproduces the source's truck-to-box relative orientation: generated demos rotate the wrist 40 deg median (p90 101 deg) while carrying, humans 3 deg; the box accepts any truck yaw, so this rotation is unnecessary. Policy failures after lifting (71% of failures) come with 4-10x larger rotation commands. Also source-demo quality matters: TA demos (regrasps, pushing the truck) give 18% generation success vs 44% for our clean demos. How do MimicGen-family methods choose object frames / transforms, handle symmetric or task-irrelevant pose components, select source segments, and filter or weight generated data? What is known about how source-demo quality and generated-data quality drive policy success?

tracks.title: 행동·관측 표현 (연구 축 C)
tracks.question: Training actions are Mimic labels = (target EE pose - current EE pose), clamped to +-1, which includes the controller's tracking lag: |dx| p90 0.127, rotation up to 1.0 rad/step, idle 0.8%; human keyboard actions are only -0.05/0/+0.05 with 20% idle. The policy issues large rotation commands right after lifting and then stalls 16-20 cm short of the box. Observations are absolute poses in the robot base frame; the truck has a 180 deg grasp symmetry and the box accepts any yaw. What does the literature say about action representation for BC (delta vs absolute pose, relabeling generated actions, action normalization/clipping, rotation parameterization, smoothing) and observation representation (object pose relative to the end-effector, symmetry-canonicalized orientation), and which of these could become a one-factor experiment here?

tracks.title: 정책 구조와 폐루프 강건성 (연구 축 D)
tracks.question: Many failures are marginal: on the same start state (eval seed 42 fixes start states per rollout index) both training seeds fail 18 times (11.5 expected if independent) but only one fails 32 times, and the same checkpoint gives different per-rollout outcomes on two GPUs. The dominant failure is a decisive, wrong gripper 'open' (outputs are +-1) while the truck is still 16-20 cm from the box (18 of 68), plus slips during fast wrist rotation (10). The policy is robomimic BC-RNN GMM (LSTM, 10-step context, hidden state reset every 10 steps, 5 GMM modes, low-noise eval). What evidence exists that action chunking / temporal ensembling, diffusion or flow policies, transformer/longer history, separate gripper heads or gripper-as-classification, phase/progress conditioning, or DAgger-style corrective data reduce such compounding errors and premature gripper decisions in low-dim manipulation BC, and which fits our rules and 5-day budget?
